evidenceFreshness.basis: Newest run_date across the committed client-compat envelopes; deterministic by design so the drift gate stays byte-stable (see #2897).

noSurface.reason: Validation-layer gate applied across several existing MCP/spec routes rather than a distinct route of its own; see ai.spec-apply and ai.grounding for the gated route surfaces.

Honua Server is stateless and runs no backup automation of its own; base backups/WAL archiving are owned by the deployment's infrastructure layer. honua-terraform parameterizes managed-database backups (for example RDS automated backups/snapshots and multi-AZ) and documents the backup/restore drill procedure. A bring-your-own-database deployment delegates backup automation entirely to the customer's managed database. No server-side background job or HTTP route performs backups; see docs/guides/deploy/backup-and-restore.md in this repo for the server-side operator guidance that exists today.

There is no cache-state backup/restore feature in this server today (verified: no producer ever records a Redis-snapshot backup; the legacy BackupKind.RedisSnapshot enum value was removed as dead code in #2946). Redis persistence (RDB/AOF) and any cache backup/restore is an infrastructure-layer concern the deployment owns, not a server capability.

Honua Server does not evaluate or trigger failover; promoting a standby and cutting over connections is owned by the deployment's infrastructure/managed-database layer (for example RDS Multi-AZ automated failover), with the drill procedure documented in honua-terraform. A bring-your-own-database deployment delegates failover entirely to the customer's managed database. The Honua.Core FailoverDecisionEvaluator was a pure, unit-tested but uncalled evaluator with no consumer anywhere in the codebase; it was removed as dead code in #2946 rather than being (falsely) counted as the surface behind this key.

Honua Server computes no RTO/RPO posture; recovery-point/recovery-time evidence comes from the infrastructure layer's backup/restore and failover drills, captured against honua-terraform's dr-evidence-template.json schema. A bring-your-own-database deployment's RTO/RPO is defined by the customer's managed database, not by this server. The Honua.Core RecoveryReadinessEvaluator was a pure, unit-tested but uncalled evaluator with no consumer anywhere in the codebase; it was removed as dead code in #2946 rather than being (falsely) counted as the surface behind this key.
GeoArrow is selected with f=arrow on the shared FeatureServer query route and is proven by the formatter/query conformance tests; it has no separate route.
Provider failover is a configuration behavior of the geocoding.forward/reverse routes, not a distinct route.
Claims-to-role mapping is an OIDC configuration setting under identity.oidc admin routes, not a distinct route.
Multi-provider configuration is a setting on the identity.oidc admin routes, not a distinct route.
Server plugin/extension SDK is a compile-time, AOT-safe registration surface, not an HTTP route.
Layout template selection is a parameter on the printing.pdf-output GPServer route, not a distinct route.

Experimental Databricks is selected behind shared FeatureServer/OGC routes only when both provider gates and configuration are enabled; the provider has no distinct route and remains off by default for 2026.1.

Experimental Redshift is selected behind shared FeatureServer/OGC routes only when both provider gates and configuration are enabled; the provider has no distinct route and remains off by default for 2026.1.

Experimental Snowflake is selected behind shared FeatureServer/OGC routes only when both provider gates and configuration are enabled; the provider has no distinct route and remains off by default for 2026.1.

Cloud storage provider selection (AWS S3 / Azure Blob) is process-startup dependency-injection wiring driven by configuration/environment variables (for example HONUA_STORAGE_PROVIDER; see FileStorageServiceCollectionExtensions.AddCloudFileStorage), not a request-time HTTP route. Verified: no LicenseGate call checks this entitlement key anywhere in the codebase. Paid-tier enforcement for cloud-served COG/raster delivery happens at request time through the distinct raster.cloud-cog-serving entitlement gate (CogTileResolver); raster.cloud-storage-config exists only as a descriptive FeatureCatalog entry today, not an enforced gate.
Temporal mosaic selection is a query parameter on ImageServer/raster serve routes (serve.geoservices-imageserver), not a distinct route.
DPI is a request parameter on the static-map export route, not a distinct route.
Image dimensions are a request parameter on the static-map export route, not a distinct route.
Marker/path overlay counts are a request parameter on the static-map export route, not a distinct route.
Smart style defaults apply automatically when a layer publishes; not a distinct route of their own.
Capability flag advertised for SDK/admin TimeSlider integration; no server-side route of its own.
Time-range filtering is a query parameter (time) on tile routes (serve.vector-tiles / serve.ogc-api-tiles), not a distinct route.
